newsitem.title: USA: U.S. NW transmission confusion lifts power prices.
newsitem.headline: U.S. NW transmission confusion lifts power prices.

text.p: Confusion over transmission capacity and new pricing by the Bonneville Power Administration helped boost Northwest power prices, market sources said Thursday.
Cash November COB (California-Oregon border) power was last quoted $17.50-18.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), up from $17.35-17.60 on Wednesday.
"There is new strength in the physical market--people are covering shorts or putting on length," said one Oregon trader.
He noted that confusion over the "real implications" of Bonneville's decision to begin posting separate prices for power and transmission this week is adding to the market uncertainty.
"Not only is the market confused about what Bonneville is doing, Bonneville seems to be confused," said another trader.
Since Monday, BPA has posted different prices for Northwest power deliveries vs. California border deals.
After starting out at a $2.27 per MWh premium for California deals, the spread between BPA's offers for the regions narrowed to just 75 cents for Friday's prices.
"I don't see how they can justify that to their Northwest
In addition, sources said the closure early today of the DC segment of the Pacific Intertie for voltage support studies added to the market confusion.
As previously reported, the 3,200 megawatt line, which has been de-rated to 2,000 MW since a major power outage on August 10, will be subject to further curtailments and downtime through October 20.

In addition, the 4,800 MW AC segment of the Intertie, limited to 3,200 since August 10, will be restricted to 2,000 MW during daytime hours on Monday and Tuesday and to 2,800 on Wednesday through Friday.
BPA officials confirmed Thursday that the AC line is currently accepting its full 3,200 MW capacity.
